newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen capital Grozny renamed after rebel leader.
newsitem.headline: Chechen capital Grozny renamed after rebel leader.

text.p: Chechen president Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev signed an order on Thursday renaming the regional capital Grozny in honour of late separatist leader Dzhokhar Dudayev.
Yandarbiyev, speaking at a ceremony in the devastated centre of the city, said the capital would now be known as Dzhokhar-Ghala (City of Dzhokhar).

It was not clear how the change would be viewed in Moscow, which waged a bloody military campaign for 21 months to try to stop Chechnya splitting away from Russia before signing a peace deal with the separatists last August.

"Expressing the will of the Chechen people, in the name of the great and merciful Allah, I decree that the name of the capital Grozny be changed to Dzhokhar-Ghala," said Yandarbiyev, to cheers of Allahu-Akbar (God is Great) from a crowd of 5,000.
They had gathered for a ceremony commemorating Dudayev, who won the posthumous title of Generalissimo earlier this week.
The charismatic, pencil-moustachioed former Soviet air force general declared his oil-rich Moslem republic along Russia's southern fringe independent in 1991.
Moscow sent thousands of troops into the territory in late 1994 but they left less than two years later after repeated humiliating battlefield setbacks.
Tens of thousands of people died in the conflict between Russia's soldiers and separatist fighters, and several hundred thousand refugees fled the fighting.
Dudayev was reportedly killed by a Russian rocket attack while standing in a field speaking on a satellite telephone in April, 1996, but few claim to seen his body.
Much of Grozny, once a thriving oil-refining centre of 400,000, was reduced to rubble during the war.

Grozny, which means "threatening" or "menacing" in Russian, was established as a riverbank fortress in 1817 by Tsarist Cossack armies who pushed southwards toward the snow-capped Caucasus mountains in an effort to control the area.
Indigenous groups such as the Chechens battled for decades before the Russians gained an uneasy toehold in the region.
